title: Cluster 02 Drill — Gene Expression and Its Control
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 2 · 9 questions · 118 marks · cumulative over Cluster 1 + Cluster 2 + Book 1
los_html:
Learning outcomes, against the questions that test them.
2(a) structure and roles of DNA and RNA (mRNA, tRNA, rRNA)Q2, Q4
2(c) transcription, pre-mRNA to mRNA, translationQ1, Q2, Q3, Q4, Q8
2(i) i chromatin level: histone modification, DNA methylationQ5, Q9
2(i) ii transcriptional level: control elements and transcription factorsQ6, Q9
2(i) iii post-transcriptional level: splicing, polyadenylation, 5' cappingQ3, Q9
2(i) iv translational level: half-life of RNA, initiation of translationQ7, Q9
2(i) v post-translational level: biochemical modification, protein degradationQ8, Q9
reach-back 2(b) replication and its enzymes (Cluster 1)Q1
reach-back 2(d) and 2(h) DNA packing and non-coding DNA (Cluster 1)Q5, Q6, Q3
reach-back Core Idea 1 protein structure and enzymes (Book 1)Q1, Q4, Q8

Two traps here carry measured failure rates from real examiner reports: the alternative-splicing rules in Q3(a), answered correctly by only 33.12% of the cohort, and the mitochondrial code count in Q2(a), where candidates count codons rather than peptide bonds. LO 2(i) is the largest outcome in Book 2 - 234 questions in the bank, 95 at the hardest tier - and it names five levels. A pass that covers three has covered 60% of it, so Q9 is the one to sit last and sit properly.

RNA interference is cut. No learning outcome in Core Idea 2 mentions miRNA, siRNA, Dicer or RISC, so no question here needs it and it is never a valid answer at the translational level.
